issues.description: The problem statement and UML specify Rideable.messageOnRide() with no parameters and describe the returned string as "Riding on [Animal Type] [name]". The template's Main() (commented example) calls messageOnRide() with no arguments. However, the solution implements Rideable.messageOnRide(int speed) and the implementing classes (Pig, Seal) provide messageOnRide(int speed). This parameter mismatch between the specification/template and the solution will confuse students about the required method signature and prevents directly using the provided example code or following the UML.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Rideable.messageOnRide signature consistent across all artifacts. Preferably revert the solution to match the problem statement/UML: define Rideable.messageOnRide() with no parameters and update Pig and Seal implementations to return "Riding on [Animal Type] [name]". Alternatively, update the problem statement, UML and template examples to require a speed parameter and document the changed behavior consistently.

issues.description: The Rideable method signature is inconsistent across artifacts: the problem statement and template expect a no-argument messageOnRide() returning a String (and the template's Main calls r.messageOnRide() with no parameters), but the solution defines Rideable.messageOnRide(int speed) and implements messageOnRide(int) in classes (Pig, Seal). This mismatch prevents students from mapping the required interface method to the provided solution and the starter code usage.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Rideable interface and its implementations consistent with the problem/template: change Rideable.messageOnRide(int speed) in the solution to messageOnRide() (no parameters) and update Pig/Seal implementations to return the required string form (e.g., "Riding on Pig Doodle"). Alternatively, if the speed parameter is intended, update the problem statement and template (Main) to specify and call messageOnRide(int) consistently. Aligning the solution to the problem/template (no-arg) is recommended.
